name: Saat-Aath
description: Saat-Aath is a two-player Indian trick-taking game in the 3-2-5 family. A 30-card pack is used, the non-dealer calls trumps, and players contest 15 tricks with quotas of 7 for the dealer and 8 for the non-dealer.
deck: 30-card stripped deck (8-A in all suits plus 7 of hearts and 7 of spades)

overview.description: Saat-Aath is a two-player Indian trick-taking game in the 3-2-5 family. A 30-card pack is used, the non-dealer calls trumps, and players contest 15 tricks with quotas of 7 for the dealer and 8 for the non-dealer.
overview.deck: 30-card stripped deck (8-A in all suits plus 7 of hearts and 7 of spades)

history.origins: Saat-Aath is a two-player adaptation of the South Asian three-player quota game 3-2-5.
timeline: Traditional play: Develops in India as a compact head-to-head quota game.
Modern documentation: Published in English on international card-game references.
Present: Taught through online rule pages and Hindi-language video explainers.
history.cultural: The game uses the term 'hands' for tricks in Indian play culture and remains recognizable as a local skill game with bluff and memory elements.
history.evolution: Compared with 3-2-5, Saat-Aath changes to two players and uses a tableau-plus-hand structure that creates 15 tricks from a short initial hand.

setup.players: Exactly 2 players; dealer alternates by deal.
setup.deck: Start from 52 cards and remove all 2-6 plus 7 of clubs and 7 of diamonds. Trumps rank: 7 of hearts (highest), 7 of spades, then A K Q J 10 9 8 of trump suit. Non-trump suits rank A K Q J 10 9 8.
setup.dealing: Dealer gives 5 hand cards to each player. Non-dealer calls trump. Dealer then deals 5 face-down table cards in a row to each player and places 1 face-up card on each stack, giving each player 15 playable cards over time.
setup.equipment: 30-card pack and optional score sheet for match play.

rules.objective: Win enough tricks relative to your role quota: dealer targets more than 7, non-dealer targets more than 8, and 7-8 exact is a tie.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Lead**: Non-dealer leads first trick. 2. **Follow suit**: Second player must follow suit if possible from hand or currently face-up table cards. 3. **If void**: Any available card may be played; trumps can cut. 4. **Trick winner**: Higher card of same suit wins, otherwise trump wins, otherwise first played card wins when neither card is trump. 5. **Card availability**: You may play from hand or any face-up table card; when a face-up table card is played, its face-down undercard is revealed for future tricks. 6. **Continuation**: Winner of each trick leads next. 7. **End**: After 15 tricks, compare trick totals against quota thresholds.
keyRules: 7 of hearts and 7 of spades are always top trumps when special-sevens rule is used.
Those two sevens count as trumps, not as hearts/spades for follow-suit in non-trump suits.
Second hand must follow suit if able; otherwise may discard or trump.
Exact 7 tricks for dealer and 8 for non-dealer is a draw.
Non-dealer always chooses trump after the initial 5-card deal.

strategy.basic: Plan for trick timing: preserve high trumps and reveal-table opportunities for late control, not only early trick gains.
strategy.intermediate: Use leads to test whether opponent can follow suits from visible table cards, then exploit known voids with trump cuts.
strategy.advanced: Track both hidden undercards and spent trumps; winning quota margins matter in variants with next-deal card advantage.
tips: Do not expose your only control suit too early unless it secures initiative.
When leading from a face-up table card, consider delaying the reveal until trick resolution where permitted.
Role matters: dealer and non-dealer have different thresholds, so risk appetite should differ.

variations.name: No Special Sevens
variations.description: 7 of hearts and 7 of spades lose permanent trump privilege and become normal low cards of their printed suits.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes trump treatment; no engine constant overrides documented yet.

variations.name: Winner Draw Advantage
variations.description: As in some 3-2-5 circles, previous winner draws cards from loser before next deal according to margin over quota.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Draw-advantage rule is procedural; no engine overrides captured in schema yet.

scoring.description: Each deal is resolved by trick totals versus asymmetric quotas (dealer 7, non-dealer 8).
scoring.winCondition: Dealer wins by taking more than 7 tricks; non-dealer wins by taking more than 8; exactly 7-8 is tied.

synthesis.shortDescription: A two-player quota trick game with special-sevens trumps and layered table-card reveals.
